title: BackendCallFn type alias hardcodes 4-arg closure signature — adds-a-param breaks all ClosureHandler call sites
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs:349-350 — public type alias:

    pub type BackendCallFn<B, C> =
        dyn Fn(Arc<B>, String, serde_json::Value, C) -> HandlerFuture + Send + Sync + 'static;

The signature is a `dyn Fn(...)` taking exactly four args:
backend, call_id, args, caller. Every consumer that uses ClosureHandler
writes closures matching this exact signature, e.g. in
register_*_handlers macros across extension *-server crates:

    Box::new(|backend, call_id, args, caller| {
        Box::pin(async move { ... })
    })

What callers cannot depend on:

1. That additional context can be threaded through ClosureHandler
   later without rewriting every closure. Concrete candidates:
   - The handler's registered `method` name (currently dropped on
     the floor in ClosureHandler::call: lib.rs:407-417 takes
     `_method: String`, then call_fn does NOT receive method).
     The trait method takes both method and call_id, but
     ClosureHandler forwards only call_id. Documented at lib.rs:343-345.
   - A tracing span (for distributed tracing).
   - A timeout or deadline.
   - A cancellation token (once the cancellation gap from the
     existing finding ↑ Dispatcher::dispatch doc:185-227 is closed).

2. That the closure signature can evolve. A `dyn Fn` is structurally
   typed — adding a parameter is a breaking change to every
   callsite.

What goes wrong when this stays as-is:

- The first new field needed (the method name, e.g. for tracing
  span attributes) cannot be threaded through ClosureHandler
  without:
   a. Adding a new field to ClosureHandler (non-breaking under
      #[non_exhaustive]) AND
   b. Adding a new type alias BackendCallFnWithMethod alongside
      the existing one AND
   c. Forking ClosureHandler::call to accept either alias.
  …or breaking the BackendCallFn signature.

- The kit currently swallows the method name parameter
  (lib.rs:410 `_method`) silently when handlers are registered
  via ClosureHandler. This is a maintainer-known limitation but
  is invisible from the BackendCallFn signature.

Resolution paths (one is sufficient):

- Convert BackendCallFn from a Fn(...) -> HandlerFuture alias to
  a sealed trait BackendCall<B, C> with a single method `call(&self,
  cx: BackendCallContext<B, C>) -> HandlerFuture`, where
  BackendCallContext is a #[non_exhaustive] struct that can grow
  fields non-breakingly. The closure-form usage stays similar:

    BackendCall::call_fn(|cx| Box::pin(async move {
        // use cx.backend, cx.method, cx.call_id, cx.args, cx.caller
    }))

  via a blanket impl for `Fn(BackendCallContext<B, C>) -> HandlerFuture`.

- Add a parallel type alias `BackendCallFnV2<B, C>` that includes
  method and use it from a new `ClosureHandler::new_with_method`
  constructor. Keep the original alias and constructor for back-compat.
  (Less invasive but pushes the cost into "two ways to do it".)

- Document the locked-in signature on the type alias itself with
  a `# Stability` section: "this signature is locked; if you need
  more context inside the closure, drop down to a manual
  JmapHandler impl".

The current state silently drops the method name (a real piece
of context most production handlers want for tracing). The
context-struct approach makes future additions cheap and surfaces
the currently-dropped field today.
